description: Roman re-use of the hillfort and long mound next to the White Horse. The Neolithic long mound was re-used as a cemetery, the hillfort shows evidence of feasting, and just to the west a Bronze Age ring ditch was enclosed and had a burial inserted. The RSRB suggests the site had a religious focus and marks it as a 'shrine', but it is unclear if they have any specific structure in mind. all of this activity is mostly dated to the 4th CE, but some early Saxon burials were found.
bibliography: Martyn, Blick, Brindle, and et al. “Uffington (Oxfordshire).” The Rural Settlement of Roman Britain: an online resource, 2015. https://doi.org/10.5284/1030449.
Miles. “Uffington White Horse and Its Landscape.” Oxford Archaeology Thames Valley Landscapes 18 (2003).
